title: AI Fixed the Bug. Can You Merge? Three PR Review Gates
description:
The two original tests passed, but splitting 100 cents allocated only 99. Follow a real patch and test run to learn how to review requirements, the diff, and regression before merging.
This is a rerunnable local demo, not a production incident or a merged PR.

v40000.text: Three people split 100 cents. Old tests passed, but the shares totaled 99.

v40001.text: Now AI submits a fix. Would you merge it immediately?

v40002.text: We'll check requirements, diff, and regression. All three must pass.

v40003.text: First, let us see how that one cent disappeared.

v40007.text: The first old test only covered an evenly divisible amount.

v40008.text: The invalid count was also rejected. Both tests were green.

v40009.text: No test covered a remainder, so the bug stayed hidden.

v40010.text: This demo uses files we actually ran, not an imagined example.

v40011.text: It shows the code passed old tests, not that the accounting was right.

v4e1000.text: These are the two tests we actually ran on the starter project.

v4e1001.text: The first splits 120 cents equally among three people.

v4e1002.text: The second expects an error for zero people.

v4e1003.text: Both pass, but neither tells us whether remainders are handled.

v40014.text: For 100 cents and three people, the starter returned 33, 33, and 33.

v40015.text: That is not a display issue; the total really is one cent short.

v40016.text: If that cent enters the books, green tests do not justify a merge.

v40017.text: Next, let us inspect the patch AI actually submitted.

v40018.text: The failure is captured in a repeatable acceptance test file.

v40021.text: I asked Claude Code to fix my own split function to meet the task.

v40022.text: It changed code and tests, and all nine of its own tests passed.

v40023.text: This was no production incident or real merged PR.

v40024.text: It is a local patch that anyone can rerun.

v40025.text: It is useful for review practice, not evidence of a product incident.

v40028.text: Gate one: do not start with AI's completion message.

v40029.text: Write requirements as conditions you can calculate yourself.

v40030.text: The fix must preserve input rules, not just repair one example.

v40031.text: It must not silently change how the shares are assigned.

v40032.text: You should be able to state this first gate without the tool.

v40035.text: First, the output length must equal the number of people.

v40036.text: Second, all shares must add up to the original amount.

v40037.text: Third, any two shares may differ by at most one cent.

v40038.text: Fourth, when cents remain, earlier people get them first.

v40039.text: Together, those four rules define the full allocation.

v40040.text: Fixing only 100 divided by three would miss other amounts.

v4e2000.text: Testing only 100 divided by three could hard-code a special case.

v4e2001.text: Try two cents among three people: the first two should get one each.

v4e2002.text: The third gets zero, and the total remains two cents.

v4e2003.text: That case quickly exposes duplicate allocations caused by rounding.

v40042.text: The starter also had input validation.

v40043.text: The amount cannot be negative, fractional, or beyond a safe integer.

v40044.text: The count must be a safe integer from 1 through 100.

v40045.text: A patch that removes those checks fails, even if this example works.

v40046.text: They are existing rules, not optional extra credit.

v40049.text: For 100 cents and three people, expect 34, 33, and 33.

v40050.text: That checks both the total and the remainder order.

v40051.text: Checking only that each share is close is not enough.

v40052.text: Write the contract first to give the review a measuring stick.

v40053.text: For two cents and three people, the order is 1, 1, 0.

v40056.text: Gate two: open the actual diff, not just the completion message.

v40057.text: First, check that it changed only the expected code and tests.

v40058.text: Then trace 100 divided by three through the new logic.

v40059.text: Finally, check that the original protections remain.

v40060.text: A text summary can miss details. Review the diff itself.

v40063.text: This patch first computes the minimum share for each person.

v40064.text: Then it finds how many cents remain for earlier people.

v40065.text: For 100 divided by three, the base is 33 and the remainder is one.

v40066.text: The first gets one more; the others stay at 33.

v40067.text: Trace two cents among three people: the first two each get one cent.

v4e3000.text: In the full diff, the function's first two validation blocks remain.

v4e3001.text: Invalid amounts and counts are still rejected before allocation.

v4e3002.text: AI replaced average rounding with a base share and remainder.

v4e3003.text: That is the scope of this local diff, not a claim about other files.

v40070.text: I checked the original validations in the diff; they remain.

v40071.text: The file list shows only the code and tests changed.

v40072.text: New tests cover remainders, zero amount, and invalid inputs.

v40073.text: That is visible evidence, not just the tool's word.

v40074.text: If it also changed deployment or billing settings, discuss that separately.

v40075.text: Read test assertions, not just test names.

v4e4000.text: For new tests, check exactly what their assertions verify.

v4e4001.text: This patch tests that 100 split three ways yields 34, 33, 33.

v4e4002.text: It also tests two cents among five: 1, 1, then zeros.

v4e4003.text: Those cases matter more than the raw count of tests.

v40077.text: This is a local patch, not a PR someone has already approved.

v40078.text: Real projects also need module, type, and operational review.

v40079.text: The scope grows if this function connects to payments.

v40080.text: You can carry this demo method into real reviews.

v40081.text: I label this scope clearly so no one mistakes it for real approval.

v40084.text: Gate three: run the patch against a separate, later acceptance suite.

v40085.text: Tool-written tests help, but cannot be the only standard.

v40086.text: If a test did not fail on old code, it may not cover the bug.

v40087.text: So I ran the same later acceptance suite against the old code first.

v40088.text: Ideally, first reproduce the old failure, then assess the new patch.

v40091.text: The old code passed both original tests but only one of four later groups.

v40092.text: That shows the new suite catches the defect we meant to fix.

v40093.text: The patch then passed all four later acceptance groups.

v40095.text: It counters the false comfort of old exact-division tests.

v40099.text: I also ran amounts from 0 to 500 with 1 to 20 people.

v40100.text: Each case checks the total and a maximum gap of one cent.

v40101.text: These property checks catch remainder combinations you may miss.

v40102.text: The loop covers many cases, but it is not a formal proof.

v40103.text: Add business-specific cases for risks beyond this test range.

v4shot0.text: This is local acceptance output from the same patch.

v4shot1.text: Four green groups are recorded, but still compare the full diff and contract.

v4e5000.text: For every case in the loop, I checked more than the total.

v4e5001.text: It also checks output length so nobody is omitted.

v4e5002.text: It compares largest and smallest shares; the gap must be at most one.

v4e5003.text: All three assertions must hold for each case to pass this gate.

v40105.text: A zero amount must give everyone zero, not throw a strange error.

v40106.text: Negative, fractional, or huge amounts must still be rejected.

v40107.text: The same goes for zero, over 100, or fractional people counts.

v40108.text: Regression means fixing the new bug while preserving old rules.

v40109.text: Input validation is especially easy to drop during a rewrite.

v40112.text: Now put the three gates together.

v40113.text: The requirement contract defines what fixed means.

v40114.text: The diff shows which files and lines actually changed.

v40115.text: Regression tests show old and new rules hold within the tested range.

v40116.text: Miss a gate, and the review record is incomplete.

v40119.text: I put three things in the review record.

v40121.text: Second, the actual scope of the diff.

v40122.text: Third, which test failed before and passed after the patch.

v40123.text: Put those in the PR description so others can rerun the check.

v4e6000.text: Include the original failing case in the review summary.

v4e6001.text: Attach the full diff, not just two attractive core lines.

v4e6002.text: List rerun commands and the range of tests that passed.

v4e6003.text: The next reviewer can verify it instead of trusting a verbal report.

v40126.text: Passing this small task still cannot decide for a real business.

v40127.text: If the requirement was wrong, tests may pass for the wrong behavior.

v40128.text: Someone must review scope, data impact, and rollback options too.

v40129.text: The person merging must own that judgment.

v40130.text: Merging is a responsible human decision, not a model's decision.

v40133.text: In GitHub's formal flow, reviewers can comment on changed lines.

v40134.text: They can request changes or approve after reading the evidence.

v40135.text: We are not approving any real PR here.

v40136.text: The point is to let the next reviewer find the same evidence.

v40137.text: The video shows the rule, not someone else's PR as decoration.

v40140.text: Back to the start: AI fixed the bug and tests are green. Merge?

v40141.text: Check requirements, diff, and regression; then a person decides.

v40142.text: Keep the starter, patch, and tests together for this example.

v40143.text: Try this on your next small fix instead of memorizing a rule.

v40144.text: Then carry the method from this exercise into larger changes.
